articles.title_orig: Trump backs diesel deal with Russia, says 'world market suffered with high prices'
articles.title_zh: Trump backs diesel deal with Russia, says 'world market suffered with high prices'
articles.content_orig:
Retired Gen. Philip Breedlove warns Russia will use oil revenue to finance attacks while buying time at the negotiating table.
President Donald Trump's efforts to reach a diesel agreement with Russia could provide Russian President Vladimir Putin with fresh revenue to fund his war against Ukraine while allowing Moscow to buy time through negotiations it has little intention of honoring, a former NATO commander warned Sunday.
Retired Gen. Philip Breedlove , former NATO supreme allied commander Europe and head of U.S. European Command, told Fox News Digital that Washington also risks undermining Ukraine's war effort by striking a deal with what he called "the enemy."
"And so we are cutting a deal with the enemy," Breedlove said, warning that "all of this money will go into fueling Mr. Putin's continued attacks in Ukraine."
The Russian government said Saturday it had partially lifted a ban on diesel exports with immediate effect, following the new agreement between Putin and Trump for Russia to supply the U.S. and global markets, Reuters reported.
As previously reported by Fox News Digital, Trump's package calls for the release of 300,000 tonnes of diesel "to the American and global marketplace," followed by 500,000 tonnes in November and another 1 million tonnes afterward.
KATIE ZACHARIA HITS GROUND RUNNING, PROMISES TRUMP DIESEL DEAL DELIVERS CHEAPER GAS FOR AMERICANS
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy speaks during a briefing in Kyiv, Ukraine, Thursday, April 17, 2025. (AP Photo/Efrem Lukatsky)
The diesel agreement preceded Trump's announcement Sunday of what he called an " energy ceasefire " between Russia and Ukraine, with the president saying both sides had agreed to halt attacks on energy infrastructure.
"Effective immediately, there is an ENERGY CEASEFIRE in the War between Russia and Ukraine. Both parties have agreed. Do not break it!" Trump wrote on Truth Social .
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy , however, indicated that Ukraine had not been informed of a finalized ceasefire agreement but expressed willingness to halt attacks on Russian energy facilities if Moscow reciprocated. He also accused Putin of repeatedly rejecting peace proposals and continuing strikes on Ukraine's energy infrastructure.
"Ukraine has proposed many de-escalatory steps. Putin had one answer to all of them – 'nyet,'" Zelenskyy wrote on X.
"We do hope that he will finally say something to America, Ukraine, and the entire world that will lead to a real and dignified peace," he added.
Zelenskyy also said Russian forces had carried out more than 200 strikes on Ukraine's electricity generation and transmission facilities over the past week, along with 17 strikes targeting gas and oil infrastructure.
He said the attacks had killed more than 150 people and wounded more than 700 over the past week.
Trump's "energy ceasefire" announcement followed tension between Washington and Kyiv over Ukrainian drone strikes on Russian oil refineries, a component of Ukraine's strategy to weaken Moscow's ability to finance its military campaign.
UKRAINE TARGETS RUSSIA WITH OVER 1,000 DRONES, KILLING 2 AS MOSCOW HOLDS LAST DAY OF ELECTIONS
A view of Russian President Vladimir Putin in front of the Kremlin. (Reuters/Tom Szlukovenyi | Photo by Contributor/Getty Images | Fox News Digital)
Breedlove argued that Russia and Ukraine are pursuing different objectives, accusing Moscow of targeting Ukrainian civilians and critical infrastructure while describing Kyiv's attacks on Russian energy facilities as an effort to disrupt the revenue sustaining Putin's war.
"Russia is carrying on a campaign of what we call counter value. In other words, Russia is attacking the Ukrainian people and trying to force their society to separate themselves from their president, President Zelenskyy," Breedlove said.
Breedlove also predicted Washington would pressure Zelenskyy to suspend attacks on Russia's oil industry despite their strategic importance.
"What I expect will happen is the United States will force or try to force Zelenskyy to stop bombing the petrochemical business in Russia," he said.
TRUMP'S DIESEL IDEA COULD HAVE UNLEASHED A PROBLEM AMERICANS NEVER SAW COMING
Overnight, Russia launched its largest aerial assault on Ukraine since the war started as fires burned in Kyiv on May 25, 2025. (Reuters/Gleb Garanich)
Trump has vehemently criticized Ukrainian strikes on Russian refineries, arguing that they are disrupting global diesel supplies and driving up costs for American farmers and ranchers.
Meanwhile, Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent defended the administration's efforts to increase diesel supplies.
"We're going to do it with all the legal authorities we have," Bessent said Sunday on Fox News. "This is good for the American people, bringing these diesel prices down," he said of the new deal.
Separately, appearing on ABC News' "This Week," Zelenskyy offered to organize Ukrainian elections if Putin agreed to a reciprocal 60-day ceasefire, although holding a vote would face legal and logistical obstacles under Ukraine's martial law.
Breedlove also expressed deep skepticism that Putin would honor any such ceasefire, citing what he described as a pattern of Russian attacks following negotiations with Trump. "Russia has never kept a promise to this president in this war," Breedlove said.
UKRAINE'S ATTACKS ON RUSSIA ARE PUSHING PUTIN CLOSER TO NEGOTIATING TABLE, TRUMP NATO AMBASSADOR SAYS
U.S. President Donald Trump (R) greets Russian President Vladimir Putin as he arrives at Joint Base Elmendorf-Richardson on Aug. 15, 2025 in Anchorage, Alaska. The two leaders are meeting for peace talks aimed at ending the war in Ukraine. (Getty Images/ Andrew Harnik)
"He's never changed his expectations, and he's never delivered on his promises. Three out of four of the big cases, the very next day or that same night after the president and Mr. Putin talked, Mr. Putin launched huge attacks in Ukraine," Breedlove continued.
Breedlove also called for a tougher U.S. response.
"We now need an administration that leads from power. We say all the time, 'strength through power,' but when it comes to Russia, our demonstrated position is continued conflict through weakness," Breedlove warned.
CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP
"He started this war. This war is to benefit Russia, and this war is to keep Mr. Putin in power. And our administration needs to tell him to stop."
Emma Bussey is a breaking news writer for Fox News Digital. Before joining Fox, she worked at The Telegraph with the U.S. overnight team, across desks including foreign, politics, news, sport and culture.

articles.title_orig: Stock Market Today: Dow falls 170 points despite strong Goldman Sachs earnings; chip selloff deepens
articles.title_zh: Stock Market Today: Dow falls 170 points despite strong Goldman Sachs earnings; chip selloff deepens
articles.content_orig:
Chip stocks fell on Tuesday, extending a sell-off sparked by worries over artificial intelligence financing and intensifying competition.
Memory chip giant Micron slipped about 5% while other memory-related names such as SanDisk , Seagate and Western Digital also sank. SanDisk fell 5% while Seagate and Western Digital both dropped 6%.
The slide, which followed declines on Wall Street on Monday, comes as investors assessed intensifying competition from China's ChangXin Memory Technologies, or CXMT .
Over the weekend , CXMT announced significant progress in developing a new chip architecture, designed to increase memory density by packing more data into a smaller space.
CXMT is China's leading rival to the likes of Micron and South Korean heavyweights SK Hynix and Samsung Electronics . Analysts broadly see CXMT as trailing the U.S. and South Korean memory leaders, which means any advancement from the Chinese firm could add more competition to the market leaders.
"Investors are jittery and looking for excuses to take profit on AI-related stocks that have outperformed this year, especially memory stocks," said UBP's senior equity advisor Vey-Sern Ling.
"In reality, while the Chinese memory makers can potentially become a threat to global demand-supply balance over time, in the short run they continue to face technology hurdles, especially for more advanced memory like HBM," Ling told CNBC via email.
CXMT shares closed 2.8% lower in Shanghai.
Phillip Wool, chief market strategist at Rayliant Global Advisors, said CXMT's breakthrough marked a significant milestone for Chinese chipmakers , demonstrating their ability to overcome technology restrictions and potentially challenge established players sooner than expected.
But he cautioned that the market reaction appeared disproportionate to the immediate competitive threat, given that CXMT has yet to demonstrate large-scale production and continues to lag Samsung and SK Hynix in market share.
"More importantly, we're not even talking about HBM here, and the Korean chipmakers are still unquestionably dominating that space, with very little threat at all from the likes of CXMT or anyone else for the foreseeable future," Wool said.
He said the sharp sell-off reflected broader anxiety over the AI trade rather than a fundamental shift in the competitive landscape.
"I read that more as a sign of how vulnerable AI sentiment is at this moment," Wool said, warning that volatility could persist as investors reassess chip demand and how long semiconductor manufacturers can sustain their pricing power.
The chief executives of Intel and Broadcom have warned that access to capital could emerge as a major headwind to the AI boom, even as demand for computing infrastructure continues to outstrip supply.
Investors are also looking ahead to a busy week of corporate earnings and U.S. inflation data, which could provide fresh clues on the outlook for interest rates that often have an inverse correlation with growth stocks.
Adding fuel to the sell-off was a post by Tesla and SpaceX boss Elon Musk, who said China has the ability to scale production once it figures out how to manufacture something.
"When China figures out how to manufacture a product, their ability to scale is often greater than the rest of the world combined," Musk said on Monday.
European chip stocks also sank in early morning trade, with semiconductor equipment maker ASML down 3.3%, and STMicroelectronics and German chip maker Infineon both down 5%. Dutch firms BE Semiconductor and ASM International were both around 4% lower at the open.
Shares of South Korean chip giant SK Hynix, a leading supplier of high-bandwidth memory chips used in artificial intelligence applications, plunged more than 10%, while rival Samsung Electronics shed 7.4% — both hitting their lowest levels since August. SK Hynix's U.S.-listed stock was down around 5% in premarket trading.
In Japan, shares of tech-focused investment giant SoftBank Group sank 8.5%. The group, which has significant exposure to the global AI industry through its huge investment in OpenAI, led a broader retreat in Japanese semiconductor and electronics shares.
Tokyo Electron , a major supplier of chipmaking equipment, dropped 7.2%, while Advantest , which makes semiconductor testing equipment, declined 2.9%. Other Japanese technology stocks also came under pressure. Lasertec fell over 5%, Disco lost 4.7% and Renesas Electronics shed 5.9%.

articles.title_orig: Sarasota Memorial Surgeon Performs World’s First Heart Procedure Combining Two Emerging Technologies - Florida Hospital News and Healthcare Report
articles.title_zh: Sarasota Memorial Surgeon Performs World’s First Heart Procedure Combining Two Emerging Technologies - Florida Hospital News and Healthcare Report
articles.source: Florida Hospital News and Healthcare Report
articles.content_orig:
Posted by cfelixcpa | Oct 13, 2026 | SF STAT! | 0 |
Oct. 13, 2026 – Sarasota Memorial Hospital heart surgeon Jonathan Hoffberger, DO, has performed the world’s first heart procedure combining two new cardiac implants from Edwards Lifesciences to replace a failing tricuspid valve and reduce stroke risk associated with atrial fibrillation (Afib).
According to Edwards Lifesciences, the milestone procedure marks the first time its TRIFORMIS RESILIA tricuspid valve and ECLIPTIS left atrial appendage (LAA) exclusion system have been implanted together in the same patient anywhere in the world.
triformis valve medical illustration
“Patients who need heart valve surgery often have other cardiovascular conditions that increase their risk of complications,” said Dr. Hoffberger, chief of cardiovascular surgery at SMH. “By combining these two devices in a single operation, we were able to replace a diseased heart valve while also addressing a significant source of stroke risk, without requiring separate surgeries.”
The two new devices address separate but potentially serious heart conditions. The TRIFORMIS RESILIA, approved by the FDA in May 2026, is the first and only surgical implant designed specifically for replacing native or prosthetic heart valves. Surgeons previously used mitral valves for tricuspid valve replacement because there were no surgical replacement tricuspid valves approved for use. Unlike the other valves, the TRIFORMIS RESILIA is engineered to accommodate the unique anatomy of the tricuspid valve. It also incorporates advanced tissue technology designed to resist calcium buildup, a major contributor to deterioration of replacement heart valves.
The other new device, the ECLIPTIS system is designed to close the left atrial appendage, a small pouch in the upper left chamber of the heart. In patients with AFib, an irregular heart rhythm that affects millions of Americans, blood can collect in this pouch and form clots that may travel to the brain and cause a stroke. Cleared by the FDA in June 2026, the ECLIPTIS device is one of several new and evolving LAA closure systems that are increasingly becoming part of cardiac procedures.
Dr. Hoffberger is one of three cardiothoracic surgeons Sarasota Memorial’s First Physicians Group (FPG) who introduced the latest cardiac devices at Sarasota Memorial Hospital this month. On the same day as Dr. Hoffberger’s milestone procedure, fellow FPG heart surgeons Jeffrey Sell, MD, and Kristen Walker, MD, also performed combined cardiac procedures, implanting Edwards’ new stroke-prevention device in two additional patients undergoing heart surgery.
The milestone reflects Sarasota Memorial’s continued investment in advanced cardiac care and multidisciplinary approach to treating patients with complex cardiovascular conditions. The health system’s comprehensive cardiac program brings together cardiac surgeons, interventional cardiologists, electrophysiologists and other cardiovascular specialists to provide a wide range of treatments, from traditional, robotic and minimally invasive heart surgery to advanced valve replacement and repairs, and other advanced interventions and therapies for complex heart conditions.
About Sarasota Memorial Health Care System (smh.com)
Sarasota Memorial Health Care System is a regional medical center offering Southwest Florida’s greatest breadth and depth of care, with about 2,500 physicians and advanced practice providers, 11,000 employees and 2 million patient visits a year across its network of care. Sarasota County’s largest employer, the community-owned health system includes two full-service hospitals in Sarasota and Venice (and third under construction in North Port), freestanding ERs in North Port and Lakewood Ranch, a rehabilitation hospital, skilled nursing facility and comprehensive network of outpatient centers, urgent care clinics and SMH First Physicians Group primary and specialty care practices. Founded in 1925, SMH’s flagship Sarasota campus also is home to the Brian D. Jellison Cancer Institute, Cornell Behavioral Health Pavilion and Kolschowsky Research and Education Institute. Both Sarasota Memorial Hospital-Sarasota and Sarasota Memorial Hospital-Venice have earned the highest 5-Star quality ratings from the U.S. Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services (CMS). SMH-Sarasota is the only Florida hospital – and one of just 11 in the nation – to earn a perfect 5-Star rating from CMS every year since the federal rating program began in 2016.

articles.title_orig: Bank earnings takeaways: Here's how JPMorgan, Goldman, Wells Fargo and Citi performed in Q3
articles.title_zh: Bank earnings takeaways: Here's how JPMorgan, Goldman, Wells Fargo and Citi performed in Q3
articles.content_orig:
Four of the largest U.S. banks reported third-quarter results on Tuesday: JPMorgan Chase , Wells Fargo , Goldman Sachs and Citigroup .
Bank of America and Morgan Stanley will post earnings on Wednesday.
The quarter was dominated by headlines around artificial intelligence, IPO uncertainty, high fuel prices and rising borrowing costs.
The banks that reported Tuesday put up mixed results . JPMorgan, the biggest U.S. bank by assets and the largest in the world by market capitalization, posted a rare miss. Goldman Sachs, meanwhile, blew past estimates for revenue and earnings per share, led by strong equities trading.
Analyst calls for all four banks touched on the opportunities and risks associated with AI, citing robust financing demand and operational advantages, but also the threat of rogue agents.
Goldman Sachs CEO David Solomon also addressed recent reports of a CEO transition plan, and Wells Fargo CFO Mike Santomassimo joined CNBC to discuss the firm's growth and the state of the consumer.
Here's what you need to know:
Citi's analyst call is over, which means bank earnings reports for Tuesday are wrapped. Bank of America and Morgan Stanley report on Wednesday to round out third-quarter results for the major U.S. firms.
Wells Fargo's Santomassimo told CNBC that both consumers and businesses are doing "really well."
"I think despite higher gas prices, both sides of the equation have been able to really work through that," he said. "We're just not seeing any sort of cracks around delinquency trends that would lead you to believe you're going to see any near-term stress that come through, at least at least for now."
Wells Fargo CFO Mike Santomassimo told CNBC's Sara Eisen that the company's underlying results are "really good" and that the bank is seeing "continued momentum" across all of its businesses.
"As you look at the net interest margin, what that really shows is sort of this good stabilization of the underlying trends," he said. "You see the higher rate environment starting to come through in terms of helping it as you look forward, and so for us, the opportunity we have ahead of us is just as big as it was last quarter."
Citi's Fraser said on the call with analysts that macro environment conditions softened during the third quarter and that the "global economy has held up remarkably well."
"In the U.S., while much has been made of the AI boom, the consumer is still driving much of the growth," she said. "The labor market is stable, and companies remain active. Our near-term economic outlook remains positive."
She added that the bank's clients have remained "engaged" and "healthy."
Citigroup CEO Jane Fraser said on a call with analysts on Tuesday that the company is focused on reducing systemic risk while deploying AI firmwide.
"Our cyberdefense strategy is about being on the front foot, about moving fast and retaining trust," Fraser said. "We don't wait for risks to happen. We're constantly preparing and improving our defenses. We're in the business of managing risk everyday, and this is no different."
Investment banking fees at all four firms reporting on Tuesday largely held up during the third quarter, with most firms either matching or surpassing prior guidance. Still, the reports revealed declines on a quarter-over-quarter basis.
At JPMorgan, investment banking revenue was up 14% year over year but down 8% quarter over quarter. JPMorgan CFO Jeremy Barnum said the pipeline remains "very, very strong."
Goldman Sachs CEO David Solomon echoed that sentiment on his company's analyst call, while declining to say whether capital markets activity has peaked. That bank reported fees that were 21% higher from the prior year, but 5% lower than the second quarter.
"IPOs that came in September were really the result of conversations in May and June around valuation expectations. Things got a little bit softer in September," Solomon said. "The IPO market was wide open. It's just if you expected a valuation and you got something 10 %to 15% less, you might choose not to go forward, you might choose to wait."
Solomon added all the tech innovation and the AI infrastructure activity is a "real good ballast" for capital markets activity on a go-forward basis, noting that doesn't mean there won't be bumps.
Citi posted the largest quarter-over-quarter decline in the fees, at 13% down. Wells Fargo reported investment banking revenue that was down 5% from the prior quarter.
Solomon warned that the AI infrastructure boom could face a painful reset if higher borrowing costs or overbuilding undermine the economics of some data center projects.
"There is going to be a lot of financing to do, and we're going to be in the middle of that," Solomon said during the bank's third-quarter call.
"It may be that over time as the financing needs grow, that there's pressure on rates and that will affect the returns and the viability of certain projects," he said. "Not every project is going to be received as well."
For now, demand for computing power remains strong and supply has yet to catch up, Solomon said, meaning more infrastructure will be built and more financing from Goldman and others will be needed. It's impossible to predict when a reset might happen or how the technology would evolve and be deployed, he said, calling the dynamic "an unknown we have to live with."
"There will be a point in time when this recalibration resets, for sure," Solomon said. "When that does happen, of course there'll be some bumps."
Citigroup, the final bank of the morning, is beginning its conference call with executives and analysts to discuss its third-quarter earnings results.
Goldman Sachs CEO Solomon pushed back against reports of an impending transition to executive chairman, saying Tuesday that no succession process or timeline is underway at the investment bank.
Last month, news outlets cited anonymous sources that said Solomon would be replaced as CEO by Goldman President John Waldron as early as next year. The process would involve a vote by the bank's board that could happen in a matter of months, according to The Wall Street Journal.
"I just want to be clear, there is no succession transition or timeline underway at Goldman Sachs," Solomon said during the bank's earnings call.
"The board and I are singularly focused on our strategy to grow the firm and continue to serve our clients," he said.
The CEO also pointed to the firm's future growth prospects, saying his leadership team was focused on expanding the franchise and accelerating its earnings growth in the coming years.
"I have to say, at the point right now where we see the benefits of the effort that the broad team has made, I'm really enjoying the job," Solomon said.
Wells Fargo's Scharf said on the call with analysts that the AI investment cycle has become "a complicated macroeconomic force in its own right."
"Demand for semiconductors, networking equipment, power generation, data center infrastructure, cooling systems, storage, cybersecurity and advanced manufacturing equipment continue to surge," Scharf said.
"The scale of investment here increasingly resembles prior infrastructure booms, creating both significant opportunities but also risks given the significant leverage used to finance the build-out and the upward pressure on prices in selected industries and supply chains," he added.
Scharf said on the call with analysts that the company's customer base is "still strong."
"Our underwriting criteria recognize that at some point consumer credit conditions will weaken," Scharf said. "To be clear, we do not see signs of this yet, but we know that cycles are inevitable."
Wells Fargo's Scharf said on the call with analysts that the company is "devoting significant management time and resources" to building out its AI capabilities.

articles.title_orig: US Treasury yield peak still ahead as Fed likely to tighten again, PIMCO's Ivascyn says
articles.title_zh: US Treasury yield peak still ahead as Fed likely to tighten again, PIMCO's Ivascyn says
articles.content_orig:
The yield on the 10-year Treasury fell on Thursday as traders digested comments from a top Federal Reserve official along with another long-dated bond auction.
The benchmark 10-year Treasury yield was down more than 4 basis points at 5.229% after reaching its highest level since 2002 this week. The 30-year Treasury bond yield dropped more than 5 basis points to 5.602% after trading around a 24-year high recently.
One basis point is equal to 0.01%, and yields and prices move in opposite directions.
Fed Governor Christopher Waller said on Thursday that more hikes are needed to bring inflation down after around 5-and-a-half years above the central bank's 2% target, but suggested rates did not need to rise immediately.
"The hikes do not need to come at consecutive meetings," Waller told a Central Bank of Turkey forum in Istanbul. "But they should be in place in an acceptable period of time."
His comments initially sent yields higher on the day. However, rates gave back those advances after President Donald Trump said the U.S. won't attack Iran until after the November midterm election . Yields also pulled back after a solid 30-year Treasury bond auction.
The department sold $22 billion in 30-year paper, with indirect bidders — which include central banks — scooping up 72.3% of the sale. That's above a 10-auction average of 68%. Direct bidders, including institutional investors, took 20.9% of the auction, just below an average of 22%. The yield at auction ease 5.618%.
That marks the final auction of the week. The department sold $58 billion in 3-year notes on Tuesday and another $39 billion in 10-year notes.
Thursday's sale "was decent but nowhere close to as good as the 10 yr auction yesterday," wrote Peter Boockvar, chief investment officer of One Point BFG Wealth Partners.
— CNBC's Brianna Bernath contributed reporting.

articles.title_orig: New Apple TV 4K vs previous model: Here’s everything new
articles.title_zh: New Apple TV 4K vs previous model: Here’s everything new
articles.content_orig:
Apple just launched a new Apple TV 4K, the fourth generation of the product. Here’s how the new Apple TV 4K compares to the previous, third-gen model from 2022.
The new Apple TV 4K has an A19 chip, the same chip that debuted in the iPhone 17 last year.
The third-gen Apple TV 4K from 2022 includes an A15 Bionic chip that first shipped in 2021. So any sort of chip upgrade would have been a big one, but A19 is an especially sizable leap with several years worth of improvements.
Apple says the new chip “delivers up to 50 percent faster CPU performance and up to 2x faster GPU performance,” which results in “greater responsiveness, faster navigation, and smoother animations.”
A19 also has a new, dedicated AV1 decoder which enables “more efficient, high-quality streaming while using less bandwidth.”
Siri AI debuts in the new Apple TV 4K, but Apple says it’s also coming to the second and third generation models. Presumably Siri AI will be more responsive on the latest hardware with A19, but it’s great that users won’t have to upgrade just to get the new Siri.
Apple says Siri AI supports features like “personal context understanding, broad world knowledge, and the ability to take even more systemwide app actions.” Some example queries include:
One exclusive upgrade with the fourth-gen Apple TV 4K is that it includes a three-microphone array with voice isolation built right into the box itself for hands-free interactions.
This enables you to say “Siri” or “Hey Siri” to interact with the assistant. You’ll no longer have to press the button on the Siri Remote, though that’s still an option too.
The Siri Remote has been upgraded to include Find My support with Precision Finding.
If you’ve ever used Precision Finding to locate a lost AirTag or another device, you’ll know how valuable this experience should prove for the Siri Remote.
When you lose the Siri Remote, you’ll be able to get guided, step-by-step directions to its location. And thanks to a new built-in speaker, you can even play a sound on the remote to help you find it.
You can order the new Siri Remote here for $59 , it’s compatible with older Apple TV 4K models so you won’t have to buy a whole new Apple TV to get it.
If you have several HomePods in your house, or plan to invest deeply in the Apple Home ecosystem, the fourth-gen Apple TV 4K has a new surround sound feature.
Using either HomePod mini 2 or HomePod 2, Apple TV 4K will support a four-speaker surround sound experience. Apple says, “The four speakers work together with Apple TV 4K to intelligently recognize their position in the room so audio timing and levels are automatically calibrated to the space.”
You can also mix and match HomePods, as long as they’re in matching pairs. For example, you can use a HomePod 2 front pair and a HomePod mini 2 rear pair—or opt for four of the same model.
Apple used to sell Apple TV 4K in two models: one with 64GB storage and a more expensive 128GB model.
With the fourth-gen Apple TV 4K, 128GB is the standard storage configuration. There are no options to pay more for higher storage. It’s still unclear how necessary the extra storage is, but perhaps we’ll see tvOS 27’s Smart Downloads feature resurface soon.

The six new devices are part of a new Apple Home Collection , which the company codeveloped with LG Electronics and Schneider Electric.
The LG smart lock costs $349 and comes with support for Apple Home Key, allowing you to unlock your door hands-free with UWB. You can unlock the door with a PIN code, too, or by using the physical keyhole beneath the keypad.

At the center of Apple’s smart home push is Siri AI-enabled HomeView , the company’s first smart home display. You can control each of the new devices with the HomeView or other Apple products, like an iPhone.

Two adults from Central North Carolina have died from the West Nile Virus this year.
The Centers for Disease Control reports 11 more cases in the state this year.
Dr Cameron Wolfe, an infectious disease expert with Duke Health, said if you get West Nile, you probably won't know it.
Possible symptoms the CDC list s are flu-like, such as a fever with headache, body aches, joint pains, vomiting, diarrhea, or rash.
The CDC recommends preventing mosquito bites as the best way to protect yourself and loved ones.
You can also use an insect repellent, wear loose fitting shirts and pants, and avoid being outside between dusk and dawn when the mosquitoes that spread West Nile virus are most active.

articles.title_orig: The major cities found sinking across the world
articles.title_zh: The major cities found sinking across the world
articles.content_orig:
Land in major cities across the world, including Mexico City , Mexico, and Medan in Indonesia is sinking, a new global satellite survey warns.
The findings, published in the journal Nature Cities, can help identify hotspots where action is needed to reduce risks to buildings, infrastructure, and communities.
A growing body of studies has shown that human activity, particularly groundwater extraction, has led to a gradual sinking of the ground surface across major cities .
As large amounts of groundwater gets pumped out in major cities, the underground sediments lose water pressure and get compressed under the weight of buildings above them.
Aerial view shows Rocinha favela in Rio de Janeiro, Brazil, (AFP via Getty Images)
However, information on land subsidence rates remains limited for most countries, making it difficult for policymakers to identify where risks are intensifying.
Country-level studies have shown that Houston and New York City in the US as well as Shanghai and Beijing in China are facing high rates of such land subsidence.
In the latest research, scientists from Peking University in China tracked land subsidence in cities across the globe, which can damage buildings, foundations, and drainage and sewage systems, and also increase flood risks.
Researchers conducted a comprehensive analysis of high-resolution satellite data collected between 2014 and 2023 to measure land movement across 465 cities with populations exceeding one million in 107 countries.
They specifically assessed radar data collected by the European Space Agency 's Sentinel-1 satellites at different times, which enabled them to detect small millimetre-level changes in the position of the ground.
They found that parts of Mexico City recorded the fastest local sinking.
Some of these areas of the Mexican capital are sinking at about 217mm per year, though the citywide average sinking rate was 8mm per year.
The most severe sinking rates were found in Asia , with land in Medan, Indonesia, subsiding by about 33mm per year, and in Bandung in the same country by 22mm per year.
Aerial photograph shows Dhaka city's skyline (AFP via Getty Images)
Chittagong in Bangladesh and Rangoon in Myanmar also had some of the highest land sinking rates of all the countries studied.
Iran 's Isfahan city was found sinking by 11mm per year, making it one of the highest citywide median sinking rates.
"Subsidence is most severe in Southeast Asia , West–Central Asia and North America , and is evident in historically under-studied regions, including South America , Africa and Russia ," scientists wrote in the study.
"We further detect marked deceleration across many cities in Southeast and East Asia , while substantial urban areas in these regions continue to show accelerating subsidence," researchers wrote.
In comparison, land movement was generally stable in Boston , New York City , London , Beijing, Tokyo , Seoul , Sydney , Montevideo, and Naples , researchers say.
Land subsidence rates in these cities were estimated to range from 0.1 to 1.9mm per year.
Cities in developing countries generally seemed to have faster subsidence rates than those in developed countries.
In some cities, including Beijing, replenishing underground aquifers since around 2016 seems to have halted subsidence in several areas, researchers say.
"Our global maps and trend estimates provide a consistent basis for identifying hotspots and prioritizing actions to reduce subsidence-related hazards," they wrote.

articles.title_orig: Argentina seeks tribunal order against UK oil activity near Falklands
articles.title_zh: Argentina seeks tribunal order against UK oil activity near Falklands
articles.content_orig:
Exclusive: Caution urged over Javier Milei government’s ‘red notice’ requests for arrest of individuals linked to oil project
Britain has appealed to Interpol to reject Argentina’s requests for the arrest of individuals involved in a large oil project off the Falkland Islands .
With tensions over the sovereignty of the British overseas territory reaching levels not seen since the war with Argentina in 1982, UK officials have sought urgent assurances from the international organisation.
A letter has been sent to Interpol’s headquarters in Lyon arguing that “red notice” requests from Argentina for the arrest of such individuals, including British nationals, should be seen as politically motivated.
It is understood the UK government is concerned by what sources suggested was an attempt to bully people and companies out of working in the Falklands .
An oil project known as Sea Lion in the North Falkland Basin in the south Atlantic has the potential to triple the Falklands’ GDP but Argentina’s president, Javier Milei , has vowed to block it. Argentina’s strategy includes attempts to criminalise those involved in Sea Lion and deter other investors.
In its letter, the UK government has urged Interpol to be cautious in its handling of Argentinian requests for detentions, it is understood.
Andrea Clausen, the chief executive of the Falklands government, confirmed that the use of Interpol by Argentina was a threat but added: “One would hope that Interpol wouldn’t necessarily take action.”
She said: “Certainly those of us who have an interest have had a look at certain sections of Interpol’s constitution to see what we think it could mean.”
It is understood that a response from Interpol to the UK government’s correspondence stated that it would respect article 3 of its constitution, which forbids it from undertaking any intervention or activities of a political character.
Interpol screens red notices, which are requests to locate and provisionally arrest a person pending extradition. If circulated to the enforcement agencies, individual member countries then decide whether to act on the requests. Nearly 20,000 were issued last year.
The foreign secretary, Ed Miliband, has told MPs that the UK will protect businesses working in the Falklands from pressure from Argentina through measures under protection of trading interests (PTI) legislation.
The legislation allows the UK to issue orders and directions forbidding British individuals and companies from complying with specific foreign laws or trade controls. It also opens up the possibility that those affected by Argentinian legal pressure could claim damages in UK courts.
Miliband said: “The UK’s support for the Falkland Islands is steadfast. Argentina’s attempts to intimidate businesses and individuals engaged in legitimate commercial activity are unacceptable. Companies should be free to make lawful commercial decisions without the threat of political coercion.
“We will always stand up for the Falkland Islanders, their right to determine their own future, and their right to pursue legitimate economic development.”
The intensity of Argentinian pressure relating to the Falklands is at a level that UK officials say has not been seen since the war 44 years ago that followed the invasion ordered by the then Argentinian dictator, Gen Leopoldo Galtieri.
The 74-day conflict ended with the surrender of the Argentinian forces and cost the lives of 649 of its military personnel, 255 British military personnel and three Falkland Islanders.
Argentina continues to claim sovereignty over the 700 islands that make up the Falklands and has dismissed a 2013 referendum in which 99.8% of the islands’ 3,600 residents voted to remain a British territory, with only three votes against .
Despite Interpol’s reassurance about its screening of red notice requests, concerns remain that Argentina could convince the organisation’s member states that its requests are not political but rooted in domestic legislation.
after newsletter promotion
Milei has initiated criminal proceedings against the Israeli company Navitas and its British partner, Rockhopper Exploration, which are the core companies in the offshore Sea Lion project.
A draft national sovereignty bill introduced to Argentina’s congress would further expand the scope of sanctions to affiliates of those companies, financial intermediaries, shareholders and suppliers.
The bill additionally contains clauses that could target those involved in the fishing industry in the Falklands, which makes up a large part of the islands’ economy. The archipelago is 300 miles (500km) east of the southern Patagonian coast of Argentina.
Workers in the oil and fisheries sectors on the Falklands – known in Argentina as Las Malvinas – are understood to be concerned that they could be targeted should they travel, particularly to South America, where there is support for Buenos Aires’s sovereignty claim.
In a tandem move to kill off Sea Lion, Argentina is expected within 24 hours to escalate further its dispute with the UK by requesting arbitration under annex VII of the UN convention on the law of the sea (Unclos) over the oil project.
On 28 September, Milei gave the UK a two-week deadline to stop the project or face such legal action. The deadline passed on Monday and Argentinian newspapers said an application for arbitration would follow.
Under it, Buenos Aires will claim the UK is in breach of a UN resolution inviting the parties to negotiate over the sovereignty dispute and refrain from “unilateral modifications” to the situation. It will be seeking a binding ruling that the UK must stop the drilling. However, UK government sources are confident that Unclos will not wade into a sovereignty dispute.
At a public meeting on Monday evening, one of the Falkland Islands’ assembly members, Dean Dent, told constituents that the UK government was working hard on a tough response to the Argentinian Unclos threat.
“The UK government has assembled quite an in-depth team of legal advisers, KCs – that is the first step,” he said. “There have been four recent similar cases where a case of sovereignty has been taken to Unclos and all four were disregarded by the tribunal as all four cases were a sovereignty issue, not a maritime issue.”
The UK government is expected to be increasingly muscular in its approach to Argentina in the coming days. The prime minister, Andy Burnham, told parliament on Monday that he had raised the issue and “the clear and declared will of the islanders to remain British” with the US president, Donald Trump.

articles.title_orig: Rumour: GTA 6 Will Be Ported to PC in Record Time Following Its Debut on PS5
articles.title_zh: Rumour: GTA 6 Will Be Ported to PC in Record Time Following Its Debut on PS5
articles.content_orig:
Rockstar Games is known for prioritising console platforms for its games, with PC versions following many months if not years later. Well, if a new report is accurate, GTA 6 might not take very long at all to break that rule.
According to GamesBeat , the hotly anticipated open world game is coming to PC in the first quarter of 2027 — just a few months following its launch on PS5.
GTA 6 is scheduled to arrive on 19th November, 2026 for console platforms, and the report, which is based on the word of "four industry sources familiar with the studio’s plans", says it'll be available on PC within the first three months of 2027.
As mentioned, if true, this would be a much shorter turnaround than was the case for GTA 5 . After the initial launch for consoles in September 2013, the PC version followed in April 2015, a year and seven months later.
Similarly, PC players had to wait approximately an extra year for Red Dead Redemption 2 to arrive.
It's difficult to know how likely it is that this information is accurate. Rockstar typically takes longer to port its games to PC, but it's also very possible it is better prepared for GTA 6 and will have the game ready in less time than usual.
Even if it's only a few months later, I do wonder whether most people would rather pick it up for PS5 than wait for the PC version. Some will no doubt double-dip, too.
The other thing to consider is GTA Online; so far, Rockstar has said next to nothing about the new iteration of the game's online component. This is purely speculative, but I wonder if GTA 6 will arrive on PC at or around the same time that Online launches.

articles.title_orig: UNESCO hosted regional capacity-building workshop for natural World Heritage in Central Asia and Mongolia in Almaty
articles.title_zh: UNESCO hosted regional capacity-building workshop for natural World Heritage in Central Asia and Mongolia in Almaty
articles.content_orig:
The capacity-building workshop for natural World Heritage properties in Central Asia (Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan, Tajikistan, Turkmenistan and Uzbekistan) and Mongolia was held in Almaty on 7 and 8 October 2026. The two-day event aimed to further strengthen the technical capacity of site managers and national authorities to protect natural World Heritage properties, with a particular focus on transboundary cooperation.
The workshop was coordinated by the UNESCO World Heritage Centre , the UNESCO Regional Offices in Almaty and Beijing and IUCN . It was built on the 2025 capacity-building workshop held under the same project, which aims to enhance transboundary cooperation among natural and mixed World Heritage properties in Asia by strengthening existing site management, mapping knowledge and capacity gaps, and identifying further opportunities for transboundary cooperation.
The workshop was financed by the Republic of Korea through the UNESCO/Republic of Korea Funds-in-Trust project “Enhancing Transnational Cooperation and Fostering Peace: Natural and Mixed World Heritage in Asia” . The project’s donor is the Korea Heritage Service (KHS) . Russian–English interpretation was provided throughout.
Participants reviewed the concept of Outstanding Universal Value and World Heritage activities in Central Asia and Mongolia, including state of conservation, Periodic Reporting, the Upstream Process, Preliminary Assessments and nominations. They discussed how to ensure management effectiveness using tools such as Enhancing our Heritage Toolkit (EoH) 2.0 and the new 2026 Managing World Heritage Manual, and how conservation principles and governance help sustain the values and integrity of properties. State Party representatives and site managers shared experiences from Tajik National Park (Mountains of the Pamirs) , the Tugay forests of the Tigrovaya Balka Nature Reserve (Tajikistan), Western Tien-Shan (Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan and Uzbekistan), Cold Winter Deserts of Turan (Kazakhstan, Turkmenistan, Uzbekistan), Uvs Nuur Basin (Mongolia/Russian Federation) and Landscapes of Dauria (Mongolia/Russian Federation), followed by lively exchanges among the participants. Scientific research and monitoring were also on the agenda, including species as indicators of ecosystem health, monitoring needs, techniques and tools, and common challenges, alongside the IKI project “One Health in Nature Conservation in Central Asia” and its support for World Heritage properties.
Natural heritage knows no borders; its conservation requires our shared responsibility and collective commitment. Central Asia and Mongolia are home to invaluable Outstanding Universal Value and unique ecosystems.
The main tools for tackling issues are coordination, capacity building and awareness raising. These require a change in attitudes and in management approaches in our daily work.  And for this we need to establish cooperation and improve existing coordination.
A significant part of the discussion focused on transboundary conservation and management. Participants examined conservation principles and governance through case studies of the serial transnational World Heritage properties represented at the workshop, as well as other examples from Asia such as Phong Nha-Ke Bang and Hin Nam No National Parks (Lao PDR/Viet Nam). Lessons learned from the East Asian–Australasian Flyway Partnership (EAAFP) highlighted the importance of connecting people, including site managers, and building relationship and trust as the foundation of regional cooperation and conservation across borders.
Experts from ICCROM and IUCN addressed how to assess impacts on Outstanding Universal Value, including Environmental Impact Assessments (EIAs), assessing cumulative impacts through Strategic Environmental Assessments (SEAs) and the transboundary dimensions of regional impact assessments. The new GEF8 EcoLand joint IUCN-UNDP project on “ Integrated Conservation Management and Restoration of High-Value Landscapes in Uzbekistan” was presented, together with opportunities through UNESCO’s Natural Sciences programmes and the outcomes of UNCCD COP17 in Mongolia. An interactive exercise mapped networks and potential synergies, and the workshop concluded with reflections, feedback and a discussion of strategic next steps.
Representatives of each State Party shared their reflections on the workshop and highlighted potential follow-up activities, including strengthening operational capacities (e.g. harmonization of Tentative Lists, SEAs and resource mobilization) and further exploring thematic areas such as sustainable tourism, invasive species and climate change, through knowledge-sharing and exchange, as well as the development of a common communication platform. Building on the rich discussions during the workshop and with the support of the UNESCO/Republic of Korea Funds-in-Trust project, UNESCO and IUCN will continue to engage with national authorities and site managers across the region to support their ongoing efforts to safeguard the natural heritage located in the heart of Eurasia and further strengthen transnational cooperation.

articles.title_orig: Framework Laptop 12 (2026 Upgrade) Review: Intel's Core Series 3 Fixes A Key Flaw
articles.title_zh: Framework Laptop 12 (2026 Upgrade) Review: Intel's Core Series 3 Fixes A Key Flaw
articles.content_orig:
The upgraded silicon solves a major performance hurdle.
When I learned Framework was bringing Intel's Core Series 3 chips to the Laptop 12 , I was excited. I'm a fan of the kid-friendly edition of this modular, repairable machine but it had one major technical flaw. Like almost all of Framework's other laptops, it couldn't keep its chip cool enough to wring good performance out of its silicon. But Intel's new Series 3 chips are so fast and so power efficient that it may eliminate those thermal issues entirely. So, with a low power chip in one hand, and an already great (if pricey) laptop in the other, surely this is a match made in heaven.
Framework's policy of constantly iterating on components means it's not just the mainboard that's changed here. The 2026 model ships with a fingerprint scanner and backlit keyboard, correcting the omissions from the first-generation version. Naturally, all three are backwards-compatible with the earlier version, which can be upgraded for feature parity with its newer self. As usual, my focus here is just on the upgrade process and performance of those new components. If you'd like to know more, please read l ast year's full review which covers everything else .
The one other difference is Framework developed its own MPP / USI 2.0-compatible stylus. Much like the third party models it used to this point, the Framework Stylus charges over USB-C, has an 80mAh battery and weighs 15 grams. It supports 4,096 levels of pressure sensitivity and has two programmable buttons. Oh, and you can buy it in the same color as your laptop, so it's all matchy-matchy.
The first-generation Laptop 12 came with the choice of a 13th generation Intel Core i3 or Core i5 CPU. That kind of fit the general ethos of a lower-cost, lower-power machine aimed at the education, kid and the second-computer markets. Given Intel's 18A/Panther Lake/Core Series 3 chips are so much brawnier, and yet so much more power efficient, it's no surprise you can now equip this machine with a Core 7-series CPU. This time, you have the pick of the Core 3 304, Core 5 320 and a Core 7 350 — the latter of which is what I'm testing.
Naturally, the new silicon comes with some other benefits, such as the maximum RAM increasing to 64GB and the rear expansion card slots now supporting Thunderbolt 4. It's now possible to hook up an eGPU or a pair of 4K monitors to this machine, because Framework can't just cater to the kid market. After all, a big number of Laptop 12 buyers were developers and Linux users who fell in love with the 12, according to the company. Not to mention the fact that the 12 was already too pricey to be solely a children's machine, and the RAMpocalypse has not helped matters one bit.
I've got less to say about the new input cover, which is just the old one with backlit keys, and that's a good thing. Framework CEO Nirav Patel knows better than to mess with a good keyboard, and the 12 already had a rock solid one. As for the fingerprint reader, it slots into the side of the chassis where the old power button lived, and retains its wake light. One of Framework's biggest strengths has been to incorporate new technology like this without it causing any disruption to its machines.
As I said last year, Framework clearly learned a lot from the upgrade processes for the Laptops 13 and 16. The company made it far easier to tinker with the 12, eliminating ribbon cables and screws in favor of pogo pins and clips. Even if you didn't have access to the company's step-by-step, iFixit-style guides, you could probably work out how to repair this thing from sight. The one major change, if you can call it that, is that the RAM DIMM now faces up, rather than down, as found on the older board.
Swapping out the mainboard requires you to disassemble most of the machine, but don't feel daunted. Taking it all apart and putting it back together took me 13 minutes and 42 seconds, hardly a crimp in your day. Sure, I've done this enough times that it's muscle memory but it's basically a fancy Lego set with screws (or, you know, Meccano ). Compare that time to the 32 minutes it took for me to install all the new drivers and get Windows working.
One thing to note: If you don't have the foresight to download the updated Wi-Fi drivers before your install, you'll have an issue. You can either be prepared, use another machine or pick up one of Framework's ethernet adapters. I actually think the latter option is an essential purchase anyway, given the ease of throwing one into the chassis for big downloads and installations. And it'll save your bacon on those days when the Wi-Fi drivers elude you.
Last year, the Framework 12 was powerful enough to get plenty of routine stuff done, and that hasn't changed this time out. If all you want to do is write a term paper, watch YouTube or whatever else the youth do these days, it was fine. But the constrained thermals meant that as soon as it was asked to do anything even remotely strenuous, it started wheezing.
It had a surprisingly low performance ceiling, too, where it struggled to play Fortnite , surely table stakes for a computer aimed at kids. Thankfully, the power efficient, cool and muscular grunt of the Core Series 3 has taken a sledgehammer to that ceiling. This is not the same underpowered machine that went on sale for too much money over a year ago.
Fortnite hums along on high-res graphics, as does Hardspace: Shipbreaker , hardly a low-power title despite its age. The acid test, however, was Cyberpunk: 2077, which I'm delighted to say it was able to run perfectly well. Of course, it was using the lowest graphics settings available, but there wasn't a single skipped frame or stutter. I'm not a hard-nosed gaming aesthete, so I found it eminently playable, and if this was the only machine I had, I'd be happy with the performance.
Sadly, while the performance issues are solved, the usability ones aren't — at least not for heavy loads. While I've had this machine on my lap for much of testing and writing this review, I wouldn't dare to have it there while gaming. Putting this on a table to test Cyberpunk 2077 , it took less than ten minutes before the underside of the chassis was roasting.
As for battery life, I was able to wring five or so hours from a full charge while just writing and listening to Spotify. Do anything more strenuous, like gaming, and you'll find that figure starts to fall quite sharply, to the point where I'd need to plug in at the three-hour mark.
For years, the PC industry has been content dumping out leftover crap for the education and budget markets. It amuses me to think that both Framework and Apple both looked at the low end of the market and became outraged as to what they saw. The Framework Laptop 12 was one approach to tackling the issue, producing a sturdy, repairable and upgradeable machine. The MacBook Neo was the other, and while it was neither sturdy, repairable or upgradeable, it matched the 12 in the fact it was made by people who cared . Two companies, with a focus on real engineering, both trying to tackle the issue of access at the very bottom of the market.
Both, of course, were also blighted by the financial crunch caused by the AI bubble over the last few years. The Framework 12 was clearly a few hundred dollars pricier than its makers intended and the MacBook Neo contended with a price bump shortly after its debut. This is an industry wide malaise — look at the grief Valve's endured with its hardware pricing this year — and one that nudges both machines out of the markets they were conceived for.
The lowest-spec pre-built Framework 12, for instance, with a Core 3 304, 8GB RAM, 512GB SSD and four USB-C Expansion Cards costs $799. Boost that to a Core 5 320, 16GB RAM, 512GB SSD and Windows 11 Home, and that figure leaps to $1,199. articles.title_orig: Inside the iPhone Duo and 18 Pro Cooling System: Apple Engineers Reveal a Simple Trick
articles.title_zh: Inside the iPhone Duo and 18 Pro Cooling System: Apple Engineers Reveal a Simple Trick
articles.content_orig:
Getting your Trinity Audio player ready...
The iPhone 18 Pro and 18 Pro Max push the boundaries of what mobile phones can do, such as handling on-device Siri AI calculations and running computational photography algorithms to deliver the best possible images. When it's released on Oct. 23, the iPhone Duo promises similar capabilities, but in Apple's first-ever foldable. It's all made possible by the A20 Pro processor inside the latest iPhone line, a new system-on-a-chip (SoC) from Apple's engineers that brings laptop-class power to your pocket.
Developing the SoC posed a tough question for Apple. Would the same chip work in the slab-style iPhone 18 Pros and the iPhone Duo? Each has its own set of requirements and constraints, not only for the chip and its position inside the phone's chassis, but also for effective heat management. The less room there is, the more difficult it is to move heat away from the components while maintaining performance. Managing thermal conditions plays a vital role in any device, and the limited internal space of slimmer-than-ever phones—including one that folds in half—makes it particularly tricky.
I spoke with Dan Murray, Apple's vice president of silicon engineering, and Banafsheh Barabadi, senior manager of thermal product design, to learn how Apple’s engineers navigated these new challenges and squeezed even more performance from the A20 Pro across two very different iPhone designs.
Apple says the A20 Pro has an "M-class-inspired packaging design." Macs run on the company's own M-branded processors, the most current being the M5 Max and M6. These chips power Apple's MacBook Pros and Mac mini , respectively. The A20 Pro draws some of its basic design elements from the M-line chips—specifically, their layouts.
Chips designed for phones are often stacked vertically to save space in the X-Y dimensions. Real estate on the logic board is a premium. Although this method saves side-to-side space, it introduces its own issues with data flow and heat. For example, the DRAM module is often placed on top of the processor, which can slow things down.
"With all of our iPhone SoCs before A20 Pro, we used a packaging technology called package-on-package or POP," Murray told me. "And with POP packaging, the SoC and DRAM are placed in a vertical stack with the DRAM directly on top of the SoC. But it creates challenges from a thermal perspective. Since the DRAM is physically on top of the SoC, it limits the ability to extract heat from the SoC into the system. So for A20 Pro, we brought a new packaging technology to the iPhone."
Because laptop chassis have more internal space, the DRAM module can be placed next to the processor, facilitating quicker data speeds and more effective heat management. Apple follows this configuration with the A20 Pro, unstacking the DRAM module, and placing it next to the chip rather than on top of it. This is called a wafer-level multichip module, or WMCM. Though this increases the X-Y dimensions, Apple worked closely with the system team to ensure the phones' internals could support this slightly larger package.
Qualcomm made a similar design change to the placement of the DRAM module with its recently announced Snapdragon 8 Elite Extreme Gen 6 and 8 Elite Gen 6 chips. The chipmaker's claims about its performance are lofty, but we won't be able to fully test this chip until phones built around it arrive later this year.
Apple says CPU cores and other elements are often developed once within the silicon team and then customized for different devices, such as MacBooks, iPads, and iPhones. The A20 Pro is the company's first 2nm design for phones, which Murray says delivered greater transistor density, improved power efficiency, and higher performance.
The chip has two super-cores for short, bursty workloads and four efficiency cores for background tasks and sustained workloads, which Apple says equate to a 20% performance improvement. The A20 Pro adds another GPU core, bringing the total to seven and delivering a 40% gain in graphics performance. The GPU also benefits from a second-generation neural accelerator, which improves throughput by 50%.
The A20 Pro has twice as many neural engine cores as the A19 Pro, jumping from a single bank of 16 cores to two banks of 16, for a total of 32. Apple says these two engines can be used either independently or in a bonded mode that uses all 32 at once. This is critical for on-device AI calculations.
The iPhone Duo's A20 Pro variant is just slightly different. "For iPhone Duo, we added a second display engine to support simultaneous operation of the inner and outer displays," says Murray, "and with the increased CPU and GPU performance, we ensure we can deliver a smooth user experience across the displays. For the inner display, we also added support for placing the FaceTime camera behind the display."
Put this all together, and you have a very powerful chip that runs fast, handles graphics with ease, churns through algorithms in a blink—and puts out a lot of heat. Apple had to rethink its thermal management system to dissipate the high temperatures generated by the processor.
The iPhone 17 Pro and Pro Max were the first iPhones to employ vapor chambers. These assisted the phones' A19 Pro chip and moved heat from the SoC out to the rear panel, where it could dissipate. Other phone makers have turned to vapor chambers, too. RedMagic, for example, uses a 3D vapor chamber with a composite liquid metal and a fan to keep the 11S Pro gaming phone running cool.
Apple took the basics of the iPhone 17 Pros' vapor chamber design and reengineered it not only for the higher temperatures generated by the A20 Pro but also for the different chassis designs of the iPhone 18 Pros and iPhone Duo.
The phones and processor together "represent a fundamental state change in the thermal design, and it starts with a deep collaboration with the silicon team and the WMCM packaging," Barabadi told me. "For the first time, we were able to couple silicon directly to our thermal solution, and we designed the entire system around that opportunity."
Barabadi explains that Apple followed four pillars in its approach to heat management. The first pillar is the direct silicon access. Because Apple removed the DRAM from the vertical stack, "that [gave] us a direct thermal path to our next generation vapor chamber. It basically eliminates the thermal bottleneck that previously existed on all POP packaging and allows us to extract the heat from the processor far more efficiently."
The second pillar is a new material that bridges the gap between the A20 Pro and the vapor chamber. "We call it metal over foam," says Barabadi, and it "basically creates a direct thermal and mechanically compliant coupling between the SoC and the vapor chamber. It is highly effective in removing the heat, meeting the strict mechanical requirements of the system. It took us months of development to get the material properties exactly right to be able to use this material."
The third pillar is the vapor chamber itself, which has a surface area three times larger than that of the one in the iPhone 17 Pro. It also has more de-ionized water inside to cycle heat throughout the structure. In the iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max, the vapor chamber does more than simply reroute heat. "It serves as the central structural plane for the device," explains Barabadi. The battery and the logic board are mounted directly to it. "So what it does is simultaneously [act as] a primary thermal solution and the backbone of the mechanical system. And we use 80% recycled stainless steel for the strength that was required to support the internal components."
Apple didn't stop there. The fourth pillar is a new layer applied to the back of the screen to assist. "We introduced nanotwin copper as our new display metal plate material. So this piece ... is the back display plate, and what makes this unique is that it's a new type of material that provides a unique c

The first alarm app for families.
Apple also updated the Apple TV 4K today . Last updated in 2022, the Apple TV 4K’s fourth-generation update is focused on bringing an improved surround sound experience to the Apple TV, along with Siri AI. From the outside, the new Apple TV 4K looks like the old one: a nondescript black box that sits under your TV, but on the inside, the components have been upgraded. The Siri Remote has been updated too.
The updated Apple TV features Apple’s A19 chip with an AV1 decoder and three far-field microphones. The A19 chip has a faster CPU (a claimed 50% boost) and GPU (a claimed 2x improvement), which may come in handy when playing games. The microphones allow a user’s voice to be picked up by the Apple TV despite background noise, and Apple says Siri AI will enable new ways to discover what to watch on the device. It’s worth noting that Siri AI is available on the second- and third-generation Apple TV 4K, too. Other upgraded specs that are notable include Wi-Fi 7 and Bluetooth 6.
Apple has also expanded the surround sound capabilities of the Apple TV. It can now be paired with four Apple HomePod mini 2s or second-generation HomePods or two pairs of each HomePod type. As for the Siri Remote, it now supports Precision Finding and can play a sound when used with the Find My app.
The new Apple TV 4K is a steep $299, which is disappointing but understandable given the update and 128GB of storage and can be preordered now in the U.S. and 29 other countries, with delivery and in-store availability on November 13.

articles.title_orig: Public execution opposition grows as Trump expresses private misgivings
articles.title_zh: Public execution opposition grows as Trump expresses private misgivings
articles.content_orig:
Archbishop Timothy Broglio, who oversees the Catholic Church's pastoral services to Catholics in the U.S. military, is condemning the proposed livestream of the firing squad execution of Nidal Hasan.
Broglio, in a statement Monday, also stipulated that any Catholic soldier assigned to the U.S. Army firing squad should ask to be excused from that duty, which he described as contrary to the teachings of the church. He joins other Catholic leaders in speaking out against the death penalty and the livestream plans.
Hasan, an Army psychiatrist convicted of killing 13 people in 2009 at Fort Hood in Texas, is scheduled to be executed by firing squad on Dec. 3.
Broglio recalled that he presided over the funeral of Michael Grant Cahill, the only civilian killed in that attack.
The crime committed by Hasan "was heinous, but does exposing the public to his execution serve any purpose?" Broglio asked.
"The US military generally enjoys a good reputation in the world," Broglio added. "Is there really a value to throwing them in the same boat with terrorists by broadcasting the image of the execution of a man in a wheelchair to the whole world?"

articles.title_orig: Inside Robert’s Western World: Nashville’s classic honky tonk
articles.title_zh: Inside Robert’s Western World: Nashville’s classic honky tonk
articles.content_orig:
NASHVILLE, Tenn. ( Aging Untold ) — Lower Broadway is known for high-rise honky tonks and rooftop bars that draw crowds late into the night. Under a large red boot sign sits Robert’s Western World, a bar that plays only traditional country music.
Robert’s Western World has operated for more than 30 years. The bar sells cans of beer starting at $2.50.
“We’ve left it alone. It’s not broke. Don’t fix it,” owner Emily Jones said.
Jones and her husband, JesseLee, own Robert’s Western World and are working to keep its legacy going.
“A time capsule when people walk in here,” Emily Jones said. “We are in a society where people are longing for something tangible. They want to know the history.”
JesseLee Jones moved to Nashville from Brazil and worked at Robert’s Western World before getting the chance to buy it.
“Do what’s in your heart, because if you do what’s in your heart, you don’t work a day in your life,” he said.
JesseLee Jones said the bar does not have a television inside.
“You come in here and it’s like stepping back into the 50s, and the 60s, and the 70s, the heydays of country music,” he said.
The walls are covered with photos of some of country music’s biggest names, who have been regulars at the bar, including Dolly Parton and Waylon Jennings.
“They just want to tuck in the crowd, have a beer and just be human and take in the vibe,” Emily Jones said.
The bar was named one of USA Today’s best bars in the country.
Emily and JesseLee Jones have bought the building next door and plan to expand Robert’s Western World.
“But it will still be Nashville. It will still be real,” JesseLee Jones said. “And that is what’s missing nowadays. Believability.”

Apple is getting serious about the smart home space. The company on Tuesday showed off its new Apple Home Collection, which includes a new smart deadbolt lock, video doorbell, thermostat, temperature sensor, and a range of security cameras.
The new devices are designed to work with HomeView , the company’s new smart home hub which can be used to control connected accessories and interact with Apple’s software.
This new range of smart home accessories could help Apple compete better with Amazon Ring and Google Nest, two established players in connected home security. The products will become available in December.
Apple says the devices were built in partnership with LG Electronics and Schneider Electric — an interesting move for the company, which has long sought to build and support every smart home accessory itself.
The smart lock, priced at $349.95, stands out for its support for ultra-wideband (UWB), a wireless technology that enables more precise proximity detection than traditional Bluetooth. This could allow the lock to recognize when an authorized user approaches and automatically unlock the door, reducing the need to pull out a phone or reach for a physical key.
The $249.95 wired video doorbell, meanwhile, will let homeowners see who’s outside, monitor visitors, and receive notifications when someone approaches their property. When someone rings it, a chime will sound through Apple devices like HomeView, HomePod, and HomePod mini. Users will also be notified on their iPhone or iPad.
As for the temperature sensor, it can provide insight into conditions in individual rooms, helping users identify temperature differences between areas and make adjustments.
For security, Apple is also introducing indoor and outdoor cameras, as well as a floodlight camera ($399.95) that combines exterior lighting with video monitoring. The camera lineup includes features such as live viewing, motion detection, intelligent alerts, and video storage.

articles.title_orig: From Mongolia to the world: Rotary members mobilize for World Polio Day
articles.title_zh: From Mongolia to the world: Rotary members mobilize for World Polio Day
articles.content_orig:
As World Polio Day approaches, Rotary members around the world are mobilizing their communities to raise awareness, advocate for continued commitment and help make polio history.
In Mongolia, the World Polio Day season got off to an energetic start as around 200 members of Rotary, Rotaract and Interact clubs came together for a 3.5-kilometre End Polio Walk through the Mongolian National Park.
Organized by Areas 9 and 10 of Rotary District 3450, the event brought together Rotary members from across Mongolia, joined by District Deputy Secretary Joao Francisco Pinto, who travelled from Hong Kong to take part. Before setting off, participants warmed up together with Biyelgee, a traditional Mongolian dance – bringing a distinctly local flavour to a global cause.
And Mongolia is just the beginning.
In the weeks around World Polio Day on 24 October, Rotary members and partners will come together through events and activities across the globe – each different, but united behind the same goal.
At WHO headquarters in Geneva, WHO and Rotary will bring together Rotary members, Member States, polio survivors and eradication partners for a special event featuring WHO Director-General Dr Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus and highlighting the extraordinary partnership that has brought the world to the threshold of eradication.
In Brussels, one of the city’s most famous residents will also join the effort: on 23 October, Manneken Pis will be dressed in a specially designed End Polio Now outfit, turning the iconic landmark into perhaps the world’s smallest polio eradication ambassador.
In London, parliamentarians and polio advocates will come together to keep political attention focused on finishing the job. And in Essen, Germany, Rotary members and partners will gather at the UNESCO World Heritage-listed Zollverein industrial complex to reflect on the progress made and the commitment still needed to make polio history.
These are just a few examples of activities taking place around the world – from community walks and public events to political advocacy, awareness campaigns and fundraising – demonstrating the unique role Rotary members continue to play in mobilizing communities and sustaining commitment to a polio-free world.
This year, people everywhere can also take part through the Team End Polio Challenge on Strava , turning their own walks, runs and rides into a show of support for polio eradication. Participants can also raise funds for Rotary’s PolioPlus Fund, helping support efforts to reach and protect children from polio.
Since launching PolioPlus more than four decades ago, Rotary has combined grassroots action with global advocacy and resource mobilization to help drive the world towards eradication. World Polio Day is an opportunity to celebrate that extraordinary progress – but also to remind the world that the job is not yet finished.
More than 99% of the way there is an extraordinary achievement. But when it comes to eradication, 99% is not enough.
From Mongolia to Geneva, Brussels, London and Essen – and in communities around the world – the message this World Polio Day is the same:  Together, we can make polio history.
